extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, findings, and required sanctions/procedures in a USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline final order concerning a registered patent attorney's misconduct and reinstatement. Covers jurisdiction, implicated rules, specific sanctions, and procedural steps for suspension, reinstatement, probation, and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the statutory/regulatory basis for the Office's authority to hear and act on practitioner discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code and Rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq., applies to misconduct occurring prior to May 3, 2013. The USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq., apply to misconduct occurring on or after May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which set of rules applies to alleged misconduct based on the date of the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: State bar discipline as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings and orders of state bar disciplinary proceedings (e.g., suspensions, stipulated facts, and violations of state statutes/rules) may be the factual and legal basis for USPTO disciplinary findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites State Bar Court orders and agreed facts as the basis for admitting violations of USPTO professional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) – illegal conduct involving moral turpitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in illegal conduct involving moral turpitude is a violation of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent admitted conduct (e.g., false certification to a bankruptcy court) constituting moral turpitude; such conduct supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) – conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice is prohibited under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct that undermines court or legal processes can be the basis for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.39(b) – presenting claims or defenses not warranted by law
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a claim or defense that is not warranted under existing law violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.39(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancing legally unwarranted claims or defenses may be discipline-worthy when supported by facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) – neglecting a matter entrusted to a practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting a matter entrusted to a practitioner is proscribed by 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to perform required legal services (e.g., not appearing at a hearing) supports a finding of neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.85(a)(2) – knowingly advancing an unwarranted claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly advancing an unwarranted claim is prohibited under 37 C.F.R. § 10.85(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentional advancement of claims without basis can support sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 – reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client, per 37 C.F.R. § 11.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to communicate significant developments or to act diligently supports discipline under this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(a) – collecting an unreasonable fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting an unreasonable fee violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collecting fees for services not yet performed (e.g., mortgage loan modification fees) can constitute an unreasonable fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a) – violating or attempting to violate USPTO rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating or attempting to violate the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct is prohibited under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts that are actual or attempted breaches of the rules fall under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) – public discipline by state as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State is encompassed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State public discipline can be cited as a basis for USPTO disciplinary action or as an aggravating factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i) – conduct adverse to fitness to practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office violates 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct that undermines trust in the practitioner's ability to practice before the USPTO supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory suspension term
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for a period of one hundred and eighty (180) days commencing on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies an exact suspension length and scope (patent, trademark, non-patent matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner access and credentials are revoked during suspension; respondent shall not apply for or obtain a Customer Number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requires petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic; it requires compliance with petition procedures in § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (notice obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 governs required notices to clients and other administrative obligations upon discipline (as referenced by the Final Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution requirement prior to reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall fully pay $7,347 in restitution to the aggrieved parties, as set forth in the State Bar Court Orders, prior to reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary restitution to harmed clients is a precondition to seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics School completion prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall successfully complete Ethics School, as set forth in the State Bar Court Orders, prior to reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of specified remedial education is required before candidate may be reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPRE retake and minimum score requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall retake the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination, and achieve a scaled score equal to or greater than 86, prior to reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demonstrable passing score (>=86) on the MPRE is mandated as part of reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.59 concerns procedures for finality and publication of disciplinary actions (as referenced in the Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is reinstated to practice before the Office, Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month period of probation commencing on the date of reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms of probation specified; respondent may practice during probation unless revoked or otherwise ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED procedures for suspected probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED reasonably believes Respondent violated the Agreement, Final Order, or USPTO Rules during probation, the OED Director shall: (i) issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend Respondent for up to 24 months; (ii) send the Order to Respondent at his last address of record; and (iii) grant Respondent thirty (30) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after response and consideration, OED still believes a violation occurred, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to 24 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: No stay of suspension pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to the show-cause request and Respondent seeks review of the suspension, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not automatically delay the effect of a suspension ordered by the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, underlying violations, and reinstatement/probation terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes are publicly accessible; the order includes a sample Official Gazette notice text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in (i) addressing further complaints or evidence of the same or similar misconduct, and/or (ii) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records can be used against a practitioner in subsequent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither party is ordered to pay the other's costs as part of this Agreement.
